communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis
communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

Following up on my MNDPA request and the request for payment for data access. 

The request specifically avoids asking DHS create new data, only for it to provide access to the public data in the databases segregated from information protected under the Minnesota Data Practices Act.

I understand the barriers that presents when the data is currently held within databases. I will need to use database tools either remotely or on on a MNDHS or MNIT machine.
The request offered of providing copies as a less burdensome way to comply with the obligations of the MNDPA in lieu of direct inspection.

I am reiterating my request to either have accessible remote access to the data directly or for copies to be provided free of charge. I am familiar with SQL and am happy to work with raw datasets and databases.

It's understandable that the DHS would like to avoid incurring costs. I believe providing access and working with me and others from the disability community to research the patterns the data will show, will greatly benefit the state of Minnesota through savings in case management & HCBS costs.

This isn't without precedent the Department of Health & DHS partnered with Elder Family Voices for related datasets and are providing ongoing technical support and data access for Elder Care IQ. https://eldercareiq.org/home

Elder care IQ is viewed as necessary because as "those vulnerable" we haven't had the agency, autonomy and authority ourselves to prevent abuses from happening to us and to stop them when they do. 

You can start to change that by taking this first step in partnering to create a disability lead and run disability data lab in MN. A place & platform on which  those of us who have already reached our disabled futures can work with Allies, Researchers, journalists, Policymakers and government officials all understand the disabled future we share. 

Until DHS buys into that vision. I would appreciate if you could provide access to the data free of charge as obligations under the MNDPA require.

Open roads and their skies,

Jonathan

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Louis O. Giuffrida
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to, mentioning, or generated as a result of investigation of Louis Onorato Giuffrida (October 2, 1920 – November 20, 2012), who served as director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency from May 1981 to September 1985, being forced to resign amid mounting accusations of fraud, waste, and abuse. Proof of death is not required as his death was widely reported: http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/middletownpress/obituary.aspx?n=louis-o-giuffrida&pid=161812525#fbLoggedOut

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL EMAIL] -  RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #1435964-000
communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.  Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on “Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request” on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000

Case Type:
FOIPA

Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)
The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 104 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 853 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,786 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 2,500 days for processing.

Respectfully,

Public Information Officer
FBI - Information Management Division
200 Constitution Drive
Winchester, VA  22602
O: (540) 868-4593
E: foipaquestions@fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@fbi.gov>

Do you have further questions about the FOI/PA process? Visit us at http://www.fbi.gov/foia

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov/fdps-1/@@search-fdps    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled (San Diego Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting incident-level crime data for a research project comparing neighborhood-level crime across large US cities. I am asking for the same kind of extract many departments already publish through their open data portals.

Records requested. One row per reported offense, for offenses occurring between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2025, with these fields:

the incident, case or report number
the date the offense occurred
the offense description, and the offense code if you have one
the location of the offense, as latitude and longitude

Offense fields. Whatever your system already stores is fine. Something along the lines of NIBRS offense codes and descriptions is ideal, but please do not translate, recode or reclassify anything on my behalf. I am not asking you to do any work beyond exporting the fields as they sit. If your records hold more than one offense description or classification per record (for example a local code, a UCR or NIBRS code, and a plain-text description), please include all of them rather than choosing between them.

Location. If coordinates cannot be released, I will accept a block-level address instead - either "4200 BLOCK OF WYOMING ST" or an address with the house number masked to the hundred block, for example "42XX WYOMING ST". I am not asking for exact street addresses. Several large departments publish location in exactly this masked form, and it is sufficient for my purposes.

No personal information is requested. I am not asking for the name, address, date of birth, race, sex, age or any other identifying detail of any victim, witness, suspect, arrestee or officer. Please withhold all such fields. I am asking only for what the offense was, when it happened, and roughly where.

Format. CSV, or any delimited or database export your records system produces. One file for the whole period is easiest, but annual files are fine.

Cost. Please send me a written estimate before incurring any charge above $50.

If any part of this cannot be released, please release the rest and tell me what was withheld and why.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Mummolo

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: DFR Use and Operations (Reno Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the flight path information related to any operations that occurred over or within 0.25 Statute Miles of 10 N Virginia Street Reno, 89501 between the dates of 07/10/2026 and 07/23/2026. The minimum data needed is:
- Minimum operating altitude within that radius
- Maximum operating altitude within that radius
- The UAS platform used (i.e. Skydio X10, BRINC Responder, etc.)
- System attachments equipped during operations (i.e. parachute, deployable floatation device, etc.)

An export of the flight logs is acceptable if this request as stated would require the creation of new documents. These flight logs are easily downloaded from the Fleet Management page of the respective fleet software. Data about the purpose of the flights may be anonymized, and this data can be filtered prior to export to ensure it is responsive only to the requested area and dates.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Jenkins

communications.subject: RE: Nevada Public Records Act Request #P025739-072626
communications.communication:
Good morning,

I have reached out via phone as well, but want to share this resource across to the Records Division. I understand the cited reason for delaying responding to this request is staffing constraints. This effort should take 1 person approximately 15 minutes to gather the requested information. This information can be accessed by any individual at Reno PD that has a Skydio Cloud sign in.

Following the instructions in this article shared by Skydio, all requested records can be easily filtered and gathered with all requested information contained in that data set:

https://support.skydio.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402745384475-How-to-use-Fleet-Manager-in-Skydio-Cloud

The ease of use of this tool, and the extremely limited scope of the request should not require 2 months to provide. This request does not require the generation of any additional records, as these flights should already be logged and stored as mandated by the Certificate of Authorization or Waiver with the FAA that these operations occur under. This information can be requested by the FAA at any time, and must be stored to be compliant with FAA regulations, meaning that no new records should be required to be produced.

It is hard to believe that staffing issues are this significant a constraint when the Reno PD accounts for more than a third of the city spending. If action is not taken soon, a judicial remedy will be required as permitted under NRS 239.011.

I look forward to receiving the requested information promptly.

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Vancouver Public Schools District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

 RCW 42.56.230(2) Personal information is exempt from public inspection and copying under this chapter, including information about a student enrolled or previously enrolled in a local education agency (LEA), in any records pertaining to the student, including correspondence. Personal information of family members or guardians of a child who is subject to exemption if the family member or guardian resides at the same address as the child and disclosure of the family member’s or guardian’s information would result in disclosure of the personal information of child.  
 Records withheld include student identifiable information, as well as all educational records protected from disclosure, with the exception of directory information, that are maintained in a file for that student. In this instance, redactions discuss the students individualized educational program, and placemnt, as well as IEP evaluations.  The names and email address of the student's parents are also redacted under FERPA. With the submission of this information, we believe we have fully complied with your request and we will close the file. The District desires to provide you with the fullest assistance possible.  If you believe this response does not fully comply with your public records request, please reply to this email to ask any follow up questions within five (5) business days. Please be advised that Public Records Act one (1) year statute of limitations to seek judicial review has started to run because the District does not intend to further address this request. Sincerely, Jen Anderson 
Paralegal

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide the following records in electronic form:





The complete, fully executed contract or agreement currently governing STA’s student transportation services.
All amendments, addenda, renewals, extensions, replacement agreements, and change orders associated with the contract.
All exhibits, schedules, scopes of work, service-level requirements, performance standards, route or fleet requirements, and other incorporated documents.
All pricing, rate sheets, payment terms, fuel-cost provisions, escalation formulas, incentives, credits, and other compensation-related terms.
All provisions or attachments addressing insurance, indemnification, bonding, data access, cybersecurity, student safety, reporting, records retention, subcontractors, audit rights, termination, and renewal options.
Records sufficient to show the contract’s original effective date, current expiration date, available renewal terms, and current status.
Any District approval, board action, award notice, renewal approval, or other record authorizing or approving the contract, its amendments, or its renewals.


The requested date range is January 1, 2014 through the date this request is processed. If the District maintains multiple agreements or contract versions during that period, please provide each responsive version rather than only the most recent document.

Please provide the records by email or electronic download. If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions and identify the specific legal basis for each withholding. If the District does not maintain a requested record, please identify the office or entity believed to maintain it, if known.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Irving Brown
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry of Irving Brown (November 20, 1911 - Feburary 10, 1989), a prominent labor leader and anti-communist activist. Proof of death is not required as his date of birth was over 100 years ago. Cross-references to Brown can likely be found in records on:

-Thomas Wardell Braden
-David Dubinsky
-Jay Lovestone
-Walter Reuther
-Victor Reuther

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. This is also to include any responsive records held in offsite locations, such as the Alexandria Records Center. Please include both investigatory and non-investigatory records in your search. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Cecil County Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Cecil County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Cecil County Sheriff's Office. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Cecil County Sheriff's Office, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Cecil County Sheriff's Office data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Cecil County Sheriff's Office policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Cecil County Sheriff's Office audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Cecil County Sheriff's Office personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Cecil County Sheriff's Office.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Cecil County Sheriff's Office or by third party who make the information available to Cecil County Sheriff's Office. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Cecil County Sheriff's Office’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

i.	Sheriff’s Office compliance with this policy and state and federal laws.
ii.	Personnel with access to and use of ALPR data have been properly screened and trained.
iii.	The Sheriff’s Office has adequate procedures related to the use of the ALPR system, and that queries and information obtained through the system are conducted, shared, and/or disseminated for legitimate law enforcement purposes.
4.	Information regarding the training that Cecil County Sheriff's Office personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Cecil County Sheriff's Office or by third party who make the information available to Cecil County Sheriff's Office.
